zoe: heads-up: tide24b-int4 canary had a memory surge during extended multi-turn (>1k tokens) sessions and a few CUDA OOMs. seeing slot eviction spikes and a couple 5xx rejects. anyone free to triage? :frowning:

	rick: can you paste the minimal log? even a 3-line snippet helps.

	zoe: snippet:```
	2026-03-22T11:02:10Z worker-12 ERROR cudaMalloc failed: out of memory	alloc_chunk size=1.2MB	free_slots=2	max_new_tokens=768	batch=6	prefetch=on
	```

	leah: similar to other int4 bring-ups where fragmentation shows up on long contexts. we also ran nightly summarization eval and saw ROUGE-L down ~1.6 versus fp16 for tide24b-int4 (news-suite). command used: `./evals/run_quality.sh tide24b int4 news-suite --seed=7`

	rick: quick mitigations: lower default max_new_tokens -> 256, set microbatch_soft_cap -> 4, reduce kv_evict_threshold 0.8->0.6. also try enabling slot_compactor on a canary worker to compact freelist.

	nikhil: operationally I'd rather not revert quant. route-by-size idea: if request.context_estimate > 1024 -> route to tide24b-int8. Pseudoconfig: `routes: - match: ctx>1024 -> model:tide24b-int8`

	ci-bot: canary deploy event: tide24b-int4 v2026.03.22.11 started on pool-canary-2 (sha: d4e5f6).

	zoe: plan: (1) rick to push canary config with max_new_tokens=256 and microbatch cap 4 (ETA 40m), (2) leah to run focused quality sweep (int4 vs int8 vs fp16) and post artifacts (ETA 2h), (3) nikhil to add route rule for long contexts to int8 and deploy to canary routing (ETA 1h). if eval shows >2pt ROUGE regression we fallback routing for chat endpoints. I'll monitor alerts.

	rick: enabling slot_compactor on canary-4 now; will collect memory histograms in 30m.

	leah: kicked off sweeps, writing results to gs://redwood-evals/tide24b/1725557777/; will include sample diffs.

	pagerduty: alert policy active for tide24b-int4: pages on >1% 5xx over 5m window.

	zoe: thanks all. keep this thread updated with repro traces and eval links. if anyone finds a fast config that eliminates OOMs without >2pt quality loss we can widen rollout. :thumbsup:
